claims.text: As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^–4–10^–2 s^–1.
HfNbTaTiZr has poor resistance to oxygen at high temperature.
A brief pack-cementation aluminizing treatment will form an ultra-thin alumina surface scale on as-cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The alumina scale produced on HfNbTaTiZr will be continuous and adherent.
The alumina scale will be self-healing.
The alumina scale will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
The external alumina coating will retard oxygen ingress and suppress the formation and propagation of deleterious oxides.
A brief aluminizing treatment can create the proposed coating without altering the bulk microstructure of HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminized alloy will exhibit lower oxygen uptake and a thinner oxide scale than untreated HfNbTaTiZr during exposure at about 1000 °C in air.
The aluminized alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility similar to that of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminized alloy will retain high-temperature yield strength similar to that of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Untreated as-cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid high-temperature oxidation.
Rapid high-temperature oxidation of untreated HfNbTaTiZr degrades its mechanical properties.
The intervention is effective only while the coating remains uniformly ultra-thin and adherent and does not induce bulk-composition changes or embrittlement.
The proposed effectiveness boundary is approximately 1000 °C, several hours of exposure, and mechanical strain rates of 10^–4–10^–2 s^–1.
